newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's SEC to tighten rules on golf shares.
newsitem.headline: Manila's SEC to tighten rules on golf shares.

text.p: The Philippine's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday it will issue a circular barring companies from selling shares in golf and country clubs without prior registration of the securities.
SEC Chairman Perfecto Yasay told reporters the regulatory body had received reports of rampant selling of profitable golf and country club shares even without prior registration and licensing.
Yasay said he has directed the money market operations department of the SEC to draw up tighter rules involving these shares.
The SEC has already sanctioned five firms that were selling unregistered shares.
The SEC chairman said there has been a growing demand for golf and country club shares and values are seen rising by an average of five to six percent monthly.
